clue.text: In composition, the coda is terminal

indicators.note: composition is putting things together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A music note: the coda is the closing part of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In composition' tells you to rearrange THE CODA; 'terminal' looks like part of the musical statement but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode where current leaves a device is one of its terminals, a synonym in electrical usage.

clue.text: Central part of Italy, or northern part of England

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for central
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: Naming an Italian region or an English county as alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two places; the first half builds the second by putting C before UMBRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county in the far north-west of England, home of the Lake District.

clue.text: Wordless American historian

parts.note: tacit means unspoken, wordless

explanation.surface: A silent American writer of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wordless American' reads as a description, but the historian is the Roman Tacitus, not American.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian, author of the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: Animal — one going between well and bottomless pit

indicators.note: going between means placed in the middle of the two other pieces

parts.note: OK means well, as in all right

indicators.note: bottomless in a down clue means the last letter goes

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: An animal falls between a well and a pit with no bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a water source but is the adverb meaning all right; 'bottomless' drops the last letter of the down entry piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Solitary sailor, capsized in river, gets clear

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
solitary means one alone

indicators.note: capsized in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: tar is a crossword word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A lone sailor, overturned in a river, gets free.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; 'capsized' suits a down clue, where the sailor reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: Sweet with hard centre swallowed by beast

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A toffee with a hard middle gets gobbled up by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a type of chewy confection, so it is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Garments worn over shoulders and heads

definitions.meaning: sleeveless cloaks hanging from the shoulders
headlands, promontories jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Clothing worn over shoulders and heads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sleeveless cloaks and headlands such as Cape Horn.

clue.text: Proud nude recollected being collected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A proud naked person, remembered being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembered but means collected again, rearranging PROUD NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounded up means gathered together, as cattle or suspects are collected.

clue.text: This reminds me doubly not singularly

indicators.note: doubly means the word is taken twice
singularly means strangely, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A keepsake reminds me twice over, not just once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singularly' seems to contrast with 'doubly', but means oddly, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake, an object kept as a reminder of something.

clue.text: Many get employment in plants

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: lots means many
use means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: Many people find jobs in factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' suggests factories, but here it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotuses are water lilies, a kind of aquatic flowering plant.

clue.text: Construction kit can come in bits

indicators.note: broken into bits, the letters are free to be reassembled

explanation.surface: A model-building set arrives in pieces in its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' scrambles CAN COME, aptly for a kit that comes in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a well-known brand of metal model-building toy set with nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Fruit encountered in fall

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A fruit is met as it drops from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, a straight synonym for a sudden drop.

clue.text: Those who keep servants

definitions.meaning: people who retain or keep possession of something
household staff kept in long service, an old word for them

explanation.surface: Employers who keep household staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people who retain things and servants retained by a household.

clue.text: Churchwarden isn't veiling French saint

indicators.note: veiling means covering up, so the answer lies concealed inside these words

explanation.surface: A church official is not hiding a French saint.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across churchwarDEN ISn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Denis is the patron saint of France and first bishop of Paris.

clue.text: Berks judge? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to assess is to judge

explanation.surface: Asking whether Berkshire might nearly be judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berks' looks like the county abbreviation for Berkshire, but here it is British slang for fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Berk is British slang for an idiot, so berks are fools, synonymous with donkeys in the insulting sense.

clue.text: Psychiatrist mature after loss

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist grows older after a bereavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the loss of stock or size, a reduction in amount.

clue.text: An unfinished shelter, terribly dry inside without water

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the other
unfinished means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a house is a shelter

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: An incomplete shelter is dreadfully dry indoors for lack of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes YDR from DRY, which goes inside the shelter word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry anhydrous describes a substance containing no water.

clue.text: Reluctant to change observation post before spring

parts.note: a hide is a shelter for watching birds
a bound is a spring or leap

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's hide is visited before the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means narrow-minded and set in one's ways, resistant to new ideas.

clue.text: Beau Brummell's first to do finery foolishly

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
foolishly suggests the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Beau Brummell, the Regency dandy, begins by dressing up absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Brummell was a famous Regency dandy, so 'Beau' seems part of his name; it is the definition. 'foolishly' rearranges DO FINERY to OYFRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: Rustic complaint after missing last bus

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the one before
missing last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: colic is a stomach complaint

explanation.surface: A country person's ailment after missing the last bus home.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic means pastoral, relating to country life.

clue.text: Americans aim at no uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: to seek is to aim at
nay means no

explanation.surface: Americans intend no rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads the two pieces bottom to top, giving YANKEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name for Americans, especially among Britons.

clue.text: Parking on line for a bit of fun

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a rank is a line, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Parking on a yellow line as a lark.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a practical joke, done for amusement.

clue.text: Scared to turn deaf ear

indicators.note: to turn means the letters are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Frightened to turn a deaf ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' rearranges DEAF EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Afeared is a dialect or archaic word meaning frightened.

clue.text: Family try playing Egmont overture on Scottish peninsula

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with
an overture is the opening, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Relatives try playing Beethoven's Egmont overture on a Scottish peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' and 'overture' suggest music; 'playing' rearranges TRY, and the overture of Egmont is its first letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Kintyre is a long peninsula in western Scotland, famed in a Paul McCartney song.

clue.text: Trick taking in an ecclesiastic

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A swindle that fools a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of a cathedral chapter, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Blues rant about officer

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier rants about the Blues, a regiment or team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BLUES RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a junior army officer below the rank of captain.

clue.text: Drinks like this turned blue

parts.note: so means like this

indicators.note: turned means read the other way

parts.note: blue means sad

explanation.surface: Drinks like this went off colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SAD to DAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodas are fizzy soft drinks.

clue.text: Drop bricks around West End

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Lego is a brand of toy bricks

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Dropping bricks around London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but it gives T, the last letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to drop it.

clue.text: A welder repaired one side of the vessel

indicators.note: repaired implies the parts are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A welder mends one side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges A WELDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side of a ship sheltered from the wind, as opposed to windward.

clue.text: Quite articulate? Only 50%

parts.note: to articulate is to utter

indicators.note: 50% means half the word is taken, here its second half

explanation.surface: Is someone articulate, or only half so?
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes LY, the second half of 'Only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly and quite both mean completely, as in quite mad.

clue.text: Island puts down pets

parts.note: Cos is a Greek island
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: On an island, animals are put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts down' and 'pets' suggest a vet, but 'pets' is a verb meaning pampers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to pamper them, synonymous with indulging them fondly.

clue.text: Dickens character in retreat that is desperate

indicators.note: something in retreat moves back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Edwin Drood is the title character of Dickens's unfinished novel
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Dickens character in flight is in a desperate state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns DROOD into DOORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-or-die effort is a desperate all-or-nothing attempt.
